title: Quant Market Brief — October 24, 2026: Cost-Aware AI & Consumer Divergence

stories.headline: Cost-aware abstention beats automatic routing in a new AI evaluation
stories.fact: An ICTAI-accepted paper evaluates frozen, calibration-selected routing policies on an IT-ticket dataset. Under its illustrative cost model, logistic regression with abstention reduced held-out test cost from 0.763 to 0.472, a reported 38.1% reduction. Calibration quality alone did not guarantee useful discrimination.
stories.inference: A no-action gate can be economically useful even without a more complex predictor.
stories.uncertainty: Results are dataset- and cost-specific; they are not trading performance or a universal threshold.
stories.why: Select abstention thresholds using validation-only execution costs, then freeze them for an untouched trading test.
stories.short: A cost-aware abstention study reports 38.1% lower held-out cost for a logistic-regression routing policy. Its thresholds and costs do not transfer directly to trading.
stories.alt: Two zero-based bars compare always-route cost of 0.763 and abstention-policy cost of 0.472 in illustrative cost units, with a 38.1% reported reduction.
stories.credit: Market State Lab; Gupta, arXiv:2610.31657v1, October 22, 2026. Illustrative IT-ticket cost model; not trading returns.

stories.headline: Institutional-trader study separates forecasting skill from liquidity provision
stories.fact: A new preprint matches institutional buy/sell executions into positions and relates profitability to horizon-matched forecasting proxies and passive-execution roles. Its regressions associate both forecasting ability and greater passive participation with higher position profitability.
stories.inference: Execution role can confound a model’s apparent signal advantage.
stories.uncertainty: Observational associations and hypothetical flow-following results are not causal proof or a reproducible retail trading edge; queue access and information timing matter.
stories.why: Log aggressive/passive roles, quote age and post-fill markouts. Compare signal quality after accounting for execution role and selection effects.
stories.short: New institutional-trader research separates forecasting proxies from passive-execution roles. Associations with profitability warrant an execution audit, not a claim of causal alpha.
stories.alt: A conceptual audit diagram links matched buy and sell executions to separate forecasting and passive-execution analyses, then to position profit and loss; no performance values are plotted.
stories.credit: Market State Lab; Hao et al., arXiv:2610.31141v1, October 22, 2026. Conceptual observational-study map; no causal claim.

stories.headline: Friday closes lower as the Dow leads losses and technology steadies
stories.fact: Friday’s Dow fell 1.23%, S&P 500 0.52% and Nasdaq Composite 0.21%. Completed ETF bars show SPY 759.97 (−0.522%) and QQQ 704.40 (−0.010%). These are different indexes and instruments, so their returns need not match.
stories.inference: Friday’s near-flat QQQ close suggests stabilization after Thursday’s sharp decline, not a confirmed recovery.
stories.uncertainty: Prior-close prices cannot establish weekend executable liquidity or Monday’s opening gap.
stories.why: Preserve Friday’s close as the reference state, then reprice futures basis, ETF spreads and options on reopening.
stories.short: Friday: Dow −1.23%, S&P −0.52%, Nasdaq Composite −0.21%; QQQ was nearly flat. Stabilization after a selloff is not proof that gap risk has cleared.
stories.alt: Three bars show October 23 close-to-close index returns: Dow minus 1.23%, S&P 500 minus 0.52%, Nasdaq Composite minus 0.21%.
stories.credit: Market State Lab; Reuters October 23, 2026 closing report. Index returns, not ETF returns or weekend quotes.

stories.headline: October sentiment stays depressed as inflation expectations rise
stories.fact: Michigan’s final sentiment index was 48.0 versus September’s 48.1. Current conditions fell to 46.7 from 50.9 while expectations rose to 48.8 from 46.3. One-year inflation expectations increased to 4.7% from 4.6%; long-run expectations rose to 3.5% from 3.4%.
stories.inference: Weak household sentiment and rising inflation expectations complicate a simple growth-versus-inflation policy signal.
stories.uncertainty: Survey attitudes are not realized spending or inflation; the final 48.0 supersedes the preliminary 46.3.
stories.why: Version preliminary and final releases separately and retain component detail rather than training on a revised headline as if it were known earlier.
stories.short: Michigan final sentiment was 48.0, with weaker current conditions but stronger expectations. Inflation expectations rose at both horizons; survey readings are not realized inflation.
stories.alt: Grouped zero-based bars compare September and October sentiment, current conditions and expectations indexes, showing divergent components.
stories.credit: Market State Lab; University of Michigan final October 2026 survey, released October 23. Index points, not percentage changes.

stories.headline: American Express raises EPS guidance; reported and adjusted growth differ
stories.fact: American Express reported revenue of 20.1 billion dollars, up 9%, and EPS of 5.42 dollars versus 4.14 a year earlier. Adjusted EPS was 4.68 dollars, up 13%, excluding the net impact of its Global Business Travel investment-sale gain and related restructuring. It raised full-year EPS guidance.
stories.inference: Premium-customer spending can remain resilient while aggregate household sentiment is weak.
stories.uncertainty: The customer base is not representative of all consumers, and reported EPS includes discrete items.
stories.why: Separate recurring growth from gains and restructuring; do not use one issuer’s results as a broad consumption proxy.
stories.short: AmEx revenue grew 9%; reported EPS rose 31% versus 13% adjusted. Separate the investment-sale/restructuring impact and avoid treating premium customers as the whole economy.
stories.alt: Grouped bars compare third-quarter 2025 and 2026 reported EPS of 4.14 and 5.42 dollars, and adjusted EPS of 4.14 and 4.68 dollars.
stories.credit: Market State Lab; American Express SEC-filed October 23, 2026 release. Reported and adjusted EPS are separate measures.
